title: Editor @tool script: trying to access runtime variable on node instance of different script type spams unclear error message "Invalid access to property or key 'runtime_var' on a base object of type 'NativeType (MyClass)'"
body:
### Tested versions

- Reproducible in: v4.3.stable.official [77dcf97d8]

### System information

Godot v4.3.stable - Ubuntu 22.04.5 LTS 22.04 - X11 - GLES3 (Compatibility) - NVIDIA GeForce GTX 860M (nvidia; 535.183.01) - Intel(R) Core(TM) i7-4710HQ CPU @ 2.50GHz (8 Threads)

### Issue description

I had a hard time debugging my tool script which was trying to access a runtime variable on some parent node.

Of course, it doesn't make sense to try to use a runtime variable at edit time, but the way the error appears is inconsistent and the error message is unclear on the real cause:

- The error message only appears when trying to access a runtime variable on a node instance of a type different than the current tool script
- Trying to access a runtime variable on `self` instance of another node with same script type will not fail. It will use the type default value instead (in my real project it uses the native default e.g. `0.0` for `float`, while in the MRP below it uses the assigned default after `=`).
- We can access `@export` vars without issue, as we should
- The error message doesn't mention that the issue happens only because we're trying to access runtime value at edit time, giving the impression that tool scripts are unable to access properties at all:

> res://path/to/script.gd:53 - Invalid access to property or key 'runtime_var' on a base object of type 'NativeType (MyClass)'.

- The [documentation](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/tutorials/plugins/running_code_in_the_editor.html) doesn't mention the importance of trying to access `@export` vs runtime vars (it's obvious to me now but I didn't realize while writing the script that the var was runtime and that tool script would not just fall back to the default value I assigned)

I would suggest to improve the error message to mention that this happens in this very specific context. So user can decide to disable part of the script at edit time with `if not Engine.is_editor_hint():`, or reversely pay more attention and use some exported var instead.

Also, I'm not sure if tool script is really meant to access runtime vars on self and instances of the same type. In some projects, the assigned default value is ignored, too, but not in the MRP... Maybe we should just also show the new error message in this case.

Finally, maybe documentation could be improved to mention this issue (I haven't opened an issue on Godot Doc yet as not sure if that's important, as users may miss that detail in the documentation but will not miss the error message).

### Steps to reproduce

I joined a MRP below, but if you want to recreate the scene from scratch:

Create a sample scene with 2 Node2D, NodeA and NodeB, each with a different script. Make them siblings for easy access.

```gdscript
# NodeA
class_name A extends Node2D

@export var exported_var_a: int = 1
var runtime_var_a: float = 5.5
```

```gdscript
# NodeB
@tool
class_name B extends Node2D

@export var exported_var_b: int = 2
var runtime_var_b: float = 10.5

func _process(_delta: float):
	if OS.has_feature("debug"):
		var a: A = $"../NodeA" # make sure they are siblings (you can also @export path to NodeA)

		print("===")
		if Engine.is_editor_hint():
			print("exported_var_b: ", exported_var_b) # OK, 2
			print("runtime_var_b: ", runtime_var_b) # OK, 10.5 (but was 0.0 in my actual project)
			print("a.exported_var_a: ", a.exported_var_a) # OK, 1
			print("a.runtime_var_a: ", a.runtime_var_a) # error
		else:
			print("exported_var_b: ", exported_var_b) # OK, 2
			print("runtime_var_b: ", runtime_var_b) # OK, 10.5
			print("a.exported_var_a: ", a.exported_var_a) # OK, 1
			print("a.runtime_var_a: ", a.runtime_var_a) # OK, 5.5
```

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

[v4.3-issue-#103325-editor-tool-script-runtime-var-error.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/18988898/v4.3-issue-.103325-editor-tool-script-runtime-var-error.zip)
